questions.q: State what is meant by the digital divide.

markPoints.concept: the gap between those with access to technology and those without
markPoints.exemplar: The gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not.

questions.example: The gap between people who have access to technology and the internet and those who do not, whether because of cost, location or skills.
questions.paraphrase: The inequality between those able to get online and those who cannot.
questions.feedback: A gap in access. Saying only 'people who do not have computers' misses that it is a comparison.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.6 Lesson 4 — Culture street, station 2: The digital divide

questions.q: A council decides to put all its services online and close its offices. Explain how this could disadvantage some residents.

markPoints.concept: some residents have no internet access or no suitable device
accept: no internet|no access|cannot afford|cannot get online|not everybody can|no computer|no device|no broadband|no connection|cost|rural|where they live|poor signal
markPoints.exemplar: Some residents have no internet access at home.

markPoints.concept: or lack the skills or confidence to use the website
markPoints.exemplar: Others do not have the skills or confidence to use a website.

markPoints.concept: so they would be unable to get a service they are entitled to
accept: cannot|unable|excluded|left out|shut out|denied|lose|miss out|no way to|entitled
markPoints.exemplar: So they would be unable to get a service they are entitled to.

questions.example: Some residents have no internet connection at home, either because they cannot afford one or because the signal where they live is poor. Others have a connection but not the skills or confidence to use a website, which is more common among older residents. With the offices closed, both groups would be left unable to get a service they are entitled to.
questions.paraphrase: Not everybody can get online, whether through cost or where they live, and some who can lack the confidence to use a site, so with nowhere to go in person those people would be shut out of services that are theirs by right.
questions.feedback: Two different reasons somebody might be excluded, and then the consequence. Access and skills are not the same barrier.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of globalisation made possible by computer technology?
options: A company employing a development team in another country and managing it remotely
A school installing a new computer room
A user encrypting their hard disk
questions.feedback: Globalisation is work and trade crossing borders because the technology makes distance matter less.
